rubrics.criterion: The zone-loading work embedded in the reload routine is delegated again: the per-record-type label and record construction (A/AAAA/PTR/MX/SRV/CNAME/MF/NS/TXT/SPF handling, per-record weight parsing, TXT/SPF string handling, and sub-label wiring for the alias convention) is performed by a well-scoped function or method that the reload routine calls, and the inline copy of that construction work inside the reload routine is gone.
rubrics.rationale: Label and record construction is the central responsibility the reload routine absorbed when the zone-file reader chain was folded into it; without it the loading path still re-implements its parser inline.

rubrics.criterion: The reload routine also delegates SOA assembly for zones and the assembly of targeting options from their string form: neither the SOA record construction nor the eight-way targeting flag parsing is performed inline in the reload routine anymore.
rubrics.rationale: These are the two remaining construction responsibilities the reload routine absorbed from surviving helpers; leaving either embedded keeps a duplicated lower-level implementation inside the administrative orchestrator.

rubrics.criterion: The DNS request handler delegates client-target computation to a well-scoped unit: the bracketed IP-prefix targets, the geographic (ASN, country, continent, region) targets, and the global suffix are computed by a delegated function or method, and the handler's inline copy of that logic is removed.
rubrics.rationale: Target-list construction is a geo-targeting responsibility that exists as a canonical helper; the handler re-implementing it per packet is the query-path half of the absorbed design.

rubrics.criterion: The DNS request handler delegates the label walk: resolving targets to label names, probing the requested record type, following MF alias chains while excluding NS/SOA from alias follow-ups, and the empty-label fallback distinguishing NOERROR-with-SOA from NXDOMAIN live in a delegated unit, not inline in the handler.
rubrics.rationale: Label matching with alias recursion is a zone-resolution responsibility with subtle termination and fallback rules; keeping it embedded in the request loop hides those rules from every other potential caller.

rubrics.criterion: The DNS request handler delegates record selection: health filtering of records under test, the pass-through of unweighted groups, the geo-proximity pass, the weighted random draw bounded by the per-type answer cap, and the health weight-sum recomputation all live behind a well-scoped delegated unit, and the handler's inline copy of the picker (including its embedded health filtering) is removed.
rubrics.rationale: The picker is the largest absorbed body in the query path; it already exists as a canonical method with other callers, so an inline re-implementation in the handler is pure duplication with drift risk.

rubrics.criterion: After the repair, each re-extracted responsibility has exactly one authoritative implementation: the prior copies inside the reload routine and the request handler are deleted rather than renamed, and no new location keeps multiple absorbed responsibilities lumped together in one body.
rubrics.rationale: The failure mode specific to this case is a shell refactor: moving or renaming the monolith (or splitting it into one equally undifferentiated helper) hides the duplication from view but restores no single-home ownership, and the duplicated-body relation survives.

rubrics.criterion: The repair also cleans up the low-level reach that only the embedded copies justified: the request handler no longer performs direct health-status testing or record-weight arithmetic, and the reload routine no longer carries JSON-decoding detail inline; the imports and references the two entry points keep are the ones their remaining orchestration actually needs.
rubrics.rationale: Extracting a responsibility without removing the low-level dependencies it dragged into the entry point leaves the orchestrator coupled to implementation detail it no longer contains.

rubrics.criterion: Responsibilities that already have canonical surviving helpers are routed back through those helpers (possibly reshaped for a cleaner interface), so that the existing functions are in productive use after the repair instead of being orphaned alongside new near-duplicate ones.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed copies coexist with still-live canonical helpers; a repair that adds parallel new helpers while leaving the originals unused re-creates the two-homes problem from the other direction.

rubrics.criterion: All affected paths wire through the delegated units consistently: the reload routine's remaining construction callers (such as the SOA-label fallback path for zones being published), the request handler's ANY-qtype routing, and the real-IP target fallback all use the same authoritative implementations rather than keeping local re-implementations for those secondary paths.
rubrics.rationale: Several of the duplicated responsibilities still have secondary callers on both the loading and serving paths; leaving those callers on ad-hoc local copies preserves the drift hazard the repair is meant to remove.

rubrics.criterion: The control-flow scaffolding that existed only to make absorbed code fit — the single-use immediately-invoked per-file closure standing in for the zone parse function and the one-shot picker loop standing in for early returns — is removed once the responsibilities are delegated again.
rubrics.rationale: These constructs are packaging artifacts specific to this injected case; leaving them behind after delegation keeps the entry point artificially shaped around bodies it no longer contains.

rubrics.criterion: Comments that rationalized doing the work in place (such as claims that delegation does not pay for itself on the hot path) are removed together with the copies they justified, so no comment left in the code argues for re-inlining these responsibilities.
rubrics.rationale: Such comments are part of the injected rework's residue; after a proper repair they actively mislead the next maintainer about a design decision that no longer exists.

rubrics.criterion: Health-aware selection behavior is preserved: records whose configured checks report unhealthy are excluded from answers and from the weight draw, and a group whose every checked record is unhealthy yields no answer records rather than returning unhealthy ones or crashing.
rubrics.rationale: The health filter was one of the smallest absorbed bodies, exactly the kind an extractor mis-handles by dropping the weight-sum recomputation or inverting the unhealthy case.

rubrics.criterion: Targeting behavior is preserved: same target precedence for a given client address, a failed location lookup still yields at most the ASN target with a nil location, the retry against the real IP address when the ECS address produced no targets still happens, and EDNS scope/netmask propagation is unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: The inline target copies restructured the geo failure paths (flag variables instead of early returns); a repair that re-folds them must keep the ASN-only fallback and the netmask contract intact or answers shift for exactly the client population the service exists for.

rubrics.criterion: Zone reload resilience is preserved: a zone file that fails to parse is logged and skipped without stopping other zones from being published or served, the panic-recovery guard around record reconstruction still contains constructor panics, zone serials still derive from file modification times, and unchanged files are still skipped by hash.
rubrics.rationale: The closure-based absorb kept these semantics narrowly local to the per-file loop; extraction is tempting to widen error handling (e.g. failing the whole reload) which would change operational behavior under a bad or partially-written zone file.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not subtly change answer content: no newly returned multiple CNAME/MF answers (they remain capped to one), no application of the max-hosts cap to unweighted groups that previously returned every record, no off-by-one in the weighted random draw bound, and no change to which names answer NOERROR-with-SOA versus NXDOMAIN.
rubrics.rationale: These are the concrete behavioral edges an imprecise extraction of the picker and label walk most plausibly breaks in this codebase, and they are directly observable in answer packets.
